maria_support: Heads-up — ACME prod reported their semantic search fell over after we rolled the new embedding model. They see stale vectors for some queries and a billing spike. Repro from customer: intermittent 400/500, sometimes returned vectors that look like old model outputs. Raised support ticket #8421 and attached logs. Anyone oncall?

alex_dev: Can you paste the exact request payload + headers (we need to see model name, cache prefix, and auth token header) and a short example of the returned vector shape?

maria_support: Pasting sanitized snippet from their repro:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-3-small-v2","input":["query1","query2"],"cache_prefix":"acme-prod:v1","batch_size":16}'```They rotated their API key yesterday at 09:12 UTC. They run a single tenant prefix per environment. Customer report: some results correspond to old model semantics.

jordan_sre: Two quick ideas: 1) If the new model changed embedding dimension (e.g., 1536 -> 2048) and dimension wasn't part of the cache key in one of the serving paths, we could either see consistent misses (recompute) or worse — accidental hits returning wrong-shaped vectors. 2) If auth rotation caused some requests to route through our fallback path (legacy compute service) that doesn’t consult the same local cache, those requests would be billed at hosted rates and could explain the spike.

maria_support: Customer says they observed "unexpected cache hits" — they saw low latency for some queries but vectors matched the older model. How would we return old vectors as hits after an upgrade?

alex_dev: There's a bug hypothesis: async batch path normalizes cache keys differently from the single-request path. In the batch path we were stripping tenant suffixes on colon (`prefix.split(":")[0]`) in a prior refactor. That can cause prefix collisions when customers use structured prefixes like `acme-prod:v1` vs `acme-prod:dev`. If a collision occurs across environments, old vectors could be served to the wrong environment. Also earlier code used `model.family` instead of `model.full_version` in the key for batched requests — so version changes could be lost.

maria_support: I pulled cache log snippets from their timeline:```[2026-06-12T09:58:12Z] cache_lookup key="acme-prod|text-embedding-3|1536|sha:abcd" hit
[2026-06-12T09:58:13Z] cache_lookup key="acme-prod|text-embedding-3|2048|sha:ef01" miss -> compute
[2026-06-12T09:58:13Z] returned_vector len=1536 (client expected 2048)
[2026-06-12T10:02:34Z] cache_lookup key="acme-prod|text-embedding-3|1536|sha:abcd" hit (from another tenant stream)```So you can see hits for 1536 vectors after they had moved to 2048.

jordan_sre: That log supports a collision story. The weird part is the hit coming "from another tenant stream" — likely caused by the prefix-splitting bug. I've reproduced locally: two clients with prefixes `acme-prod:v1` and `acme-prod:dev` end up sharing the same normalized key when the batch path strips after colon. Repro command:```# repro script (local): python repro_cross_tenant_cache.py --prefix1 "acme-prod:v1" --prefix2 "acme-prod:dev" --model text-embedding-3-small-v2 --batch 8```I created a unit test and attached a failing assertion to PR 4456.

alex_dev: PR 4456 fixes two issues: include `model_full_name` and `dim` in the cache-key hash for all serving paths, and stop truncating tenant prefixes by naive split. Deployed to canary in us-west last night. Also added a log marker `cache_origin` to distinguish local-cache vs fallback-hosted lookups so we can trace billing hits.

lisa_billing: Noted. I've opened billing investigation BLG-349 to look at the spike from 2026-06-12T09:45:00Z -> 2026-06-12T11:00:00Z. Please DM request_ids where we saw fallback-hosted routing so we can reconcile chargebacks.

maria_support: Customer also described retries after 429s — they sent a 10k-item batch, hit rate limits, retried with exponential backoff incorrectly and duplicated a bunch of requests. That likely amplified billed tokens. Logs show repeated request_ids with short intervals.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: release v2026.06.13-canary deployed to us-west-2 (sha abc123).

alex_dev: Short-term mitigations we recommended to ACME: 1) add explicit model pinning in tenant config (set `model_full_name` to include version/hash), 2) change cache_prefix to avoid colons (temporary), 3) rotate client API keys and ensure all instances use the newest key. Medium-term: our patch (PR 4456) is already rolled to canary and we’ll promote after 24h of metrics.

maria_support: Customer confirmed dev environment no longer shows cross-env contamination after we applied the canary routing rule and they updated their prefix. They'll monitor prod for 48h and asked for a billing estimate of the spike.

jordan_sre: Follow-ups: 1) Run a backfill job to invalidate any cache entries that lack `dim` in their key for tenants with confirmed contamination. 2) Add a postmortem if BLG-349 concludes the refund amount > $2k. 3) Add an alert for mismatched vector lengths in responses so support sees this sooner.

lisa_billing: I’ll sync with finance and keep the ticket updated — please drop the request_id list into BLG-349.

maria_support: Thanks all — keeping this thread open while ACME watches prod. Will update when billing outcome is confirmed. :thumbsup:
